metadata.title: A Checklist, Not an Algorithm.
metadata.subtitle: The Competitive-Brief Skill (Knowledge-Work Plugins)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude produces a competitor comparison, is it running some proprietary research algorithm, or just following a written instruction file? Lands the carry-out that competitive-brief always runs the same three moves — research, compare, flag the gaps — and never more than the SKILL.md's steps say.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude runs a hidden algorithm to research competitors. It doesn't — it follows a written checklist. So: does Claude have a special checklist for competitor research?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('algorithm' -> 'checklist') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Render params (charMs=42, jitter=26, mistakeRate=4, hesitateWithin=2, hesitateBetween=8) copied directly from the already-debugged fix on the claude-plugins-official--claude-liam-agent-development sibling — this text is nearly the same length (61 chars) as that sibling's proven-safe fixed version (60 chars), so the same parameters are used from the start rather than re-discovering the overrun failure mode.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is just a folder Claude reads before it starts working. This one is called competitive-brief. Inside is one file — SKILL.md — plain-language instructions, not a hidden algorithm. Claude reads that file, then acts on it, step by step. The file is the program.
The pipeline lives in the Steps section of that file. Claude reads each step in order and executes it. It's linear — no branching, unless a step itself says otherwise.

production_viz.label: THE PIPELINE: STEPS, IN ORDER
production_viz.caption: linear, unless a step says otherwise

beats.narration_text: competitive-brief does one job: research the competitors, then generate a positioning and messaging comparison — content gaps, opportunities, and threats. Whatever isn't spelled out in those steps, this skill simply doesn't do. Same input, same steps, every run.

production_viz.label: ONE JOB, BY DESIGN
production_viz.caption: same input, same steps, every run

beats.narration_text: competitive-brief always runs the same three moves — research, compare, flag the gaps — in the same order, every time. It only ever does what the SKILL.md's steps say to do.

props.quote: competitive-brief always runs the same three moves — research, compare, flag the gaps — in the same order, every time. It only ever does what the SKILL.md's steps say to do.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to research my competitors and generate a positioning and messaging comparison with content gaps, opportunities, and threats. Read the competitive-brief skill and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. That last part matters — asking Claude to explain the plan first shows you exactly which steps the file actually specifies.
